---
title: Execution records
---

## Overview

When Quarto runs the code in a document, it can keep what the code
produced --- each cell's outputs and each inline expression's value --- as an
**execution record**. A record lets Quarto present the document again
without running anything. `q2 preview` and hub use
this to show an up-to-date page while you edit prose, and `q2 render` can use
it to produce a page on a machine that cannot run the code.

A record is an ordinary Jupyter notebook file (`.ipynb`), whichever engine ran
the code, so other tools can read it. Each cell of the notebook is one
**unit** of the document: a code cell, or an inline expression.

::: callout-note
## Quarto writes a record only when you ask

A plain `q2 render` of a Julia or knitr document builds the record in
memory, presents the output from it, and writes nothing under `.quarto/`.
The preview keeps the records it needs on its own. `record: true`, shown
below, asks for a copy of the record under the project's `.quarto/`
directory. Hub uploads from `q2 provide-hub` still use the older format
unless you set the environment variable `QUARTO_ENGINE_RECORD_WRITE` to `1`,
while the feature is rolled out.
:::

## Keeping a copy of the record

Add `record: true` to the document's `execute` options:

````markdown
---
title: Report
jupyter: python3
execute:
  record: true
---
````

A render then also writes a copy of the record under the project's `.quarto/` directory, at
`.quarto/execution-records/<document path without extension>.ipynb`. In a
project, `reports/q3.qmd` gets `.quarto/execution-records/reports/q3.ipynb`
at the project root. A standalone document with no project gets a `.quarto/`
beside it, so `q3.qmd` gets `.quarto/execution-records/q3.ipynb`.

Two renders of the same inputs write the same bytes. Many projects ignore
`.quarto/` in version control, so a record is not something to commit; do not
expect it to be shared between collaborators until a durable use for it
exists.

## What an edit does to a record

Quarto compares a record with the document to decide whether it still
describes it:

| You edit                                             | The record is |
|------------------------------------------------------|---------------|
| prose outside cells and spans                        | still fresh   |
| the code in a cell                                   | stale         |
| a `#|` option line                                   | stale         |
| an inline expression                                 | stale         |
| a front matter key that affects execution            | stale         |

So correcting a typo in a paragraph does not re-run your cells in the preview
or in hub. Any other edit above does.

The preview also keeps a cache of its own, keyed on the whole input. A prose
edit can therefore still cause a re-run there for reasons unrelated to the
record; the table is about the record only.

## Positron's cache is a different file

[Positron](https://positron.posit.co) keeps its own cache of Quarto outputs,
in per-user storage. Quarto does not use or write that file as its record,
for three reasons: Positron's file is rewritten from a fixed set of fields, so
extra information in it is dropped; it is named after a hash of the document's
location, which Quarto cannot reproduce; and it carries a timestamp that
changes on every write, so its bytes are never stable.

Quarto reads Positron's cache only when you list `positron` (or a directory of
Positron cache files) in `execute: record-sources`, described
[next](#choosing-where-records-come-from). No command's default list includes
it. Quarto never writes to or deletes Positron's cache. Output shown from it is marked as generated, so the viewer
does not offer to edit it; see
[Outputs from an imported record](../projects/preview.qmd#outputs-from-an-imported-record).

To go the other way and give Positron a cache file built from a document's
record, use [`q2 convert`](convert.qmd).

### Setting it from the command line

`q2 preview` passes `-M` to the document's code too, so a preview can write the
copy without editing the document:

``` {.bash filename="Terminal"}
q2 preview report.qmd -M 'execute: {record: true}'
```

The copy is then written at the path above each time the preview runs the
document. Turning `record` on or off does not make a record out of date.

## Choosing where records come from

The `execute: record-sources` key lists the places where Quarto looks for a
document's record, in order. The first place that has a usable record wins;
Quarto never merges records. `q2 render`, `q2 preview`, `q2 convert`, and
`q2 provide-hub` all read the key.

Set the key in a document's front matter, in a directory's `_metadata.yml`, or
in `_quarto.yml`:

``` {.yaml filename="report.qmd"}
execute:
  record-sources: q2,engine
```

The value is one comma-separated string, not a YAML list. To set it for a
single run, pass it with `-M`:

``` {.bash filename="Terminal"}
q2 render report.qmd -M 'execute:{record-sources: "q2,engine"}'
```

Keep the braces, because `-M` does not expand dotted keys. Quote a value that
contains a comma. Without the quotes, YAML ends the value at the comma and
reads the rest as a separate key, which changes the document's settings and
makes its record look out of date. A value from `-M` overrides the document's
own.

### Entries and defaults

| Entry | Where the record comes from |
|---|---|
| `cache` | the preview's own cache of earlier runs (`q2 preview` only) |
| `q2` | the copy under `.quarto/execution-records/` that `record: true` writes |
| `positron` | Positron's inline output cache, read without starting a kernel |
| a directory path | a directory of Positron-format cache files |
| `engine` | run the code |

Each command accepts some of the entries and has a default list:

| Command | Accepts | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `q2 render` | `q2`, `positron`, `engine`, a directory | `engine` |
| `q2 preview` | `cache`, `q2`, `positron`, `engine`, a directory | `cache,q2,engine` |
| `q2 convert` | `q2`, `engine` | `q2,engine` |
| `q2 provide-hub` | `q2`, `positron`, `engine` | `engine` |

A command ignores a valid entry that it cannot use and prints a note. An
unknown entry is an error that names the valid choices.

A directory entry must be inside the project. A relative path is relative to
the file that sets the key, and a leading `/` means the project root. An
absolute path, a path that starts with `~`, or a path outside the project is
an error, as is a directory that does not exist. To use a Positron cache from
outside the project, list `positron`, or copy or link the cache into the
project. A bare word that is not one of the names is an error, so write
`./notes` for a directory called `notes`. A path that contains a comma cannot be
given.

Quarto reads the key separately for each document, so one project can mix
lists. For example, a `_metadata.yml` that sets `record-sources: q2` makes every
document in its directory use saved records, and the rest of the project keeps
the default.

Because an entry that finds nothing passes the document to the next entry, the
output can depend on whose machine renders it. With `q2,engine`, a machine that
has the saved record shows its outputs, and a machine that does not has to run
the code.

### What `q2 render` does with the list

`q2 render` only reads records. It never writes one; `record: true` does that.
With the default list, `engine`, a render runs the code, as it always has.

When you list other entries first, `q2 render` takes the first record that is
current. It counts a record as not supplied when the document's code or options
changed after Quarto recorded it, or when Quarto recorded it for a different
output format, and it moves on to the next entry.

If no entry supplies a record and `engine` is not in the list, `q2 render`
warns, shows the code cells without output, and starts no engine. With
`--strict`, the warning is an error. A document with no code cells gets no
warning.

`--no-execute` removes `engine` from the list. With `q2` in the list, a render
with `--no-execute` still shows the saved outputs and starts no engine:

``` {.bash filename="Terminal"}
q2 render report.qmd --no-execute -M 'execute:{record-sources: q2}'
```

A `--replay` render ignores the key.

::: callout-note
## A preview and a render treat a stale record differently

`q2 preview` shows a stale record, and marks the page stale so that you can
re-run it. `q2 render` treats a stale record as not supplied, because a
finished page must not show outputs that belong to different code.
:::

### What `q2 preview` and `q2 provide-hub` do with the list

`q2 preview` uses `cache,q2,engine` by default: it reuses an earlier run, then a
saved record, and runs the code only if neither has one. `q2 provide-hub` uses
`engine` alone, which is a fresh run each time, after you approve it. Leave
`engine` out and the command never runs code: a preview shows only the records
it finds, and says on the page why each place had none.

"Never run code" means no code cell, inline expression, or engine process runs.
Your document's filters, shortcodes, and includes still run, as in any preview,
and so do the project's pre-render scripts, once, when the preview starts.

A shared preview (`--share`) and `q2 provide-hub` treat the host's list as a
ceiling: the list that you set with `-M`, or the command's default. A shared
document can reorder or narrow that list, but it cannot add an entry. The host sees a warning for each entry that the ceiling
rejects. A guest of a shared preview can re-run code only when `engine` is in
the host's list and `preview.engine` is not `off`. Under `off`, `engine` in the
list is ignored with a warning.

Two things to know about `provide-hub`. A record from `q2` or `positron` is
published to everyone viewing the hub document **without** the approval prompt,
because no code runs; naming the source is how you choose to share those
outputs. And until the hosted hub can read records, publishing one needs
`QUARTO_ENGINE_RECORD_WRITE=1` in the environment; without it the record is
refused with a message that names the variable.

The preview reads its sources when it starts, not again when a file changes. A
Positron cache written after the preview started, or a new `.qmd` file, is not
seen until you restart it. With a persisted `--data-dir`, a document that was
re-run keeps the record of that run across restarts, and "Clear results" in
the editor removes a record for every collaborator without looking at the
list again.

## Limits

- A document that uses an engine that builds no execution record is stored in
  the older format. Every output is still shown, but features that read
  records may not work with it.
- A single-file book render does not use `execute: record-sources`. A chapter
  that sets the key to anything other than `engine` gets a warning, and Quarto
  runs the chapter's code.
- A preview that keeps its data with `--data-dir` stores execution records
  there. If you later open that directory with an older version of `q2`, the
  page shows "Failed to parse capture". Use a new `--data-dir`, or delete the
  old one: the older version records the file again. Edits made in the
  `--ui editor` session are not written to your files unless you pass
  `--allow-edit`, so save anything you want to keep first.
- A record from a knitr document can be exported with
  [`q2 convert`](convert.qmd), and a preview reads Positron's outputs for its R
  cells. Cells in other languages of a knitr document do not take outputs from
  Positron's cache.
- To run cells in a kernel other than Python, see
  [Running other languages with Jupyter kernels](jupyter-kernels.qmd), which
  also covers choosing a kernel and what happens when one is missing.
- Inline expressions are described in
  [Inline expressions](computations.qmd#inline-expressions).
